verdict.description: Is this project's production deployment exploitable through this advisory?

confidence.description: How well the decisive facts behind the verdict are verified.

runtime_usage.description: Question 1: where the package's code executes in production.

vulnerable_code_used.description: Question 2: is the specific vulnerable function, option or feature used?

attacker_reachable.description: Question 3: can attacker-controlled input reach the vulnerable code in production?

deployment_conditions_met.description: Question 4: do the advisory's environmental preconditions (OS, hosting, flags, versions) hold?

summary.description: 2-4 plain-language sentences: the flaw, whether this project is exposed, and the decisive reason.

evidence.description: Checkable facts. Code facts cite a repo-relative file and a line you actually read.

file.description: Repo-relative path, a searched directory/glob, or (dependency facts) / (project profile) / (advisory).

line.description: 1-based line number you saw, or null when the fact is not about a single line.

note.description: What this shows and why it matters.

exploit_conditions.description: What an attacker needs: access level, entry point, input shape, configuration.

remediation.description: The concrete fix: package, target version, direct or via which parent, breaking-change risk.

workaround.description: A concrete interim measure, or null if there is none.

suggested_action.description: Your honest recommendation; a policy makes the final decision.

suggested_action_reason.description: One sentence with the decisive reason for suggested_action.
